extracted.subtask_description: Practical and ethical guidance for businessmen/industrialists on conduct, finance, negotiation, industrial policy, and an explicit plan for philanthropic life and use of wealth. Drawn from Carnegie's memoir-style prescriptions and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tools to those who can use them (meritocratic allocation)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is but one rule among Americans--the tools to those who can use them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Americans rapidly organize and give the means of advancement (schools, churches, newspapers, brass bands, etc.) to those who will use them; opportunity should be afforded to those capable of using tools rather than distributed by hereditary rank.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independence through ownership/control
rubrics_metrics.description: A man must necessarily occupy a narrow field who is at the beck and call of others. Even if he becomes president of a great corporation he is hardly his own master, unless he holds control of the stock.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To be truly independent take steps to hold controlling interest; working for mere salary constrains freedom of action. Carnegie framed his departure from salaried employment around achieving autonomy through ownership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal integrity as guiding principle
rubrics_metrics.description: I was determined to make a fortune and I saw no means of doing this honestly at any salary the railroad company could afford to give, and I would not do it by indirection. When I lay down at night I was going to get a verdict of approval from the highest of all tribunals, the judge within.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize honest conduct over expedient gains; internal moral approval should guide business decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Courteous resignation and stewardship of goodwill
rubrics_metrics.description: On resigning: express deep regret at parting, assure continued interest in colleagues' welfare, thank employees for uniform kindness, and ask for similar support for successor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leadership includes preserving institutional goodwill when departing; Carnegie's letter to officers models how to leave with respect and foster continuity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultural education to refine judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: Visiting Europe ... one may not at the time justly appreciate the advantage he is receiving from examining the great masterpieces, but upon his return ... he will find himself unconsciously rejecting what before seemed truly beautiful, and judging productions which come before him by a new standard.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exposure to art, music, and culture enlarges appreciation and raises evaluative standards—use travel and study to improve taste and judgment applicable in business and public life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adopt technological/process innovations from expert sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Cousin 'Dod'... took our Mr. Coleman to Wigan in England and explained the process of washing and coking the dross from coal mines ... began the construction of the first coal-washing machinery in America. He made a success of it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek out domain experts and foreign practices; if validated, adopt and adapt processes locally (first-mover advantage in implementing such innovations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Turn waste into value; pursue first-mover advantage
rubrics_metrics.description: It is fine to make something out of nothing; it is also something to be the first firm to do this upon our continent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value innovations that convert previously discarded materials into profitable products; being first in such conversions yields competitive and reputational benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encourage self-reliance in employees
rubrics_metrics.description: He said 'I thought we could better ourselves.' 'Who have you with you?' 'My wife.' 'Why didn't you come first to see your relative who might have been able to introduce you here?' 'Well, I didn't feel I needed help if I only got a chance.' There spoke the true Morrison, taught to depend on himself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prize and reward initiative and self-dependence in workmen/colleagues; such traits often forecast promotion and long-term success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support measured protection early, then reduction when mature
rubrics_metrics.description: Protection has played a great part in the development of manufacturing in the United States... It had become a patriotic duty to develop vital resources... I was not sufficiently prominent in manufacturing to take part in getting the tariff established immediately after the war, so it happened that my part has always been to favor reduction of duties, opposing extremes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use protective tariffs to nurture nascent industries when necessary, but support gradual reduction of duties as domestic capacity develops; oppose extreme positions on both absolute protectionism and unrestrained free trade.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use political organizing/association contributions responsibly
rubrics_metrics.description: Certainly the manufacturers never raised any sums beyond those needed to maintain the Iron and Steel Association, a matter of a few thousand dollars per year. They did, however, subscribe freely to a campaign when the issue was Protection versus Free Trade.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Industry associations may fund collective political action prudently; contributions should be limited to necessities and specific campaigns rather than pervasive bribery.

rubrics_metrics.name: View free trade as acceptable once domestic supply suffices
rubrics_metrics.description: We could now (1907) abolish all duties upon steel and iron without injury, essential as these duties were at the beginning... Home iron and steel manufacturers have nothing to fear from free trade.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When domestic production meets demand and world markets can adjust, tariff abolition or reduction is feasible without crippling local industry; practical market dynamics will protect producers from extreme harm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refuse opportunistic collusion or betrayals of partners
rubrics_metrics.description: All these allurements I declined... Jay Gould... offered... I thanked him and said that, although Mr. Scott and I had parted company in business matters, I would never raise my hand against him.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain ethical loyalty toward former partners and avoid engaging in opportunistic maneuvers that damage prior associates' interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid speculative trading; never buy what you do not pay for or sell what you do not own
rubrics_metrics.description: I have never bought or sold a share of stock speculatively in my life... I have adhered to the rule never to purchase what I did not pay for, and never to sell what I did not own.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refrain from speculative stock-market behavior including buying on margin or short selling; favor investments you fully pay for and hold responsibly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manufacturers should avoid owning exchange-traded stock to preserve judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: For the manufacturing man especially the rule would seem all-important. His mind must be kept calm and free if he is to decide wisely the problems which are continually coming before him... Speculation is a parasite feeding upon values, creating none.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational leaders should minimize involvement in stock-exchange speculation to retain clear, long-term strategic judgment; distractions of market volatility impair decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fundraising/capital-raising tactics: prepare prospectus, engage bankers and press, stress legal security
rubrics_metrics.description: I prepared a prospectus... called upon Junius S. Morgan... sold him part of the bonds... when his lawyers were called in... a score of changes were required in the wording... I called Mr. Sampson's attention to the fact that the charter of the St. Louis Bridge Company was from the National Government... He said he would be delighted to give prominence to this commendable feature. I described the bridge as a toll-gate on the continental highway.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When raising capital: prepare a clear printed prospectus; engage influential financiers early; anticipate and accommodate legal drafting changes; use respected press figures to present reassuring legal/charter protections and frame the project in appealing public terms to lift price and market confidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be decisive and precise in negotiations/communications
rubrics_metrics.description: It was an easy matter to number the lines of the bond and then going carefully over them to state what changes, omissions, or additions were required in each line. I showed Mr. Morgan the message before sending it and he said: 'Well, young man, if you succeed in that you deserve a red mark.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When seeking contractual changes or approvals across distances, send precise, line-referenced communications to minimize ambiguity and speed resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use credit and contracts strategically in building enterprise
rubrics_metrics.description: Mr. Thomson and I contracted for the whole structure, foundation, masonry, and superstructure, taking bonds and stocks in payment... The undertaking was a splendid success in every respect, except financially. A panic threw the connecting railways into bankruptcy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leverage credit and accept bonds/stock as payment to expand operations, but be mindful of systemic risk (panics/bankruptcies) that can undermine expected returns—assess counterparty and macro risks when accepting non-cash payment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify unmet demand and create new ventures to fill scaling gaps
rubrics_metrics.description: The sleeping-car business... had gone on increasing so rapidly that it was impossible to obtain cars enough to supply the demand. This very fact led to the forming of the present Pullman Company.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize when existing suppliers/capacity cannot meet demand and consider founding or expanding ventures to supply the missing capacity—turn supply constraints into entrepreneurial opportunity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cap personal income and dedicate surplus annually to benevolence
rubrics_metrics.description: Thirty-three and an income of $50,000 per annum! By this time two years I can so arrange all my business as to secure at least $50,000 per annum. Beyond this never earn--make no effort to increase fortune, but spend the surplus each year for benevolent purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt a deliberate income cap and commit annual excess wealth to charitable purposes rather than continuous accumulation; plan the transition from accumulation to distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pursue education and literary/public engagement after accumulation
rubrics_metrics.description: Settle in Oxford and get a thorough education, making the acquaintance of literary men--this will take three years' active work--pay especial attention to speaking in public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After securing financial position, invest time in formal education and cultural-literary networks to develop informed public voice and rhetorical skills useful for later public/charitable leadership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acquire media/control of opinion to advance public causes
rubrics_metrics.description: Settle then in London and purchase a controlling interest in some newspaper or live review and give the general management of it attention, taking a part in public matters, especially those connected with education and improvement of the poorer classes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ownership or control of influential publications to shape public discourse and promote education and social improvement causes; media control seen as a lever for civic influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resign from business at a set point to devote life to elevating pursuits
rubrics_metrics.description: I will resign business at thirty-five, but during the ensuing two years I wish to spend the afternoons in receiving instruction and in reading systematically... Whatever I engage in I must push inordinately; therefore should I be careful to choose that life which will be the most elevating in its character.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt an explicit timeline to leave commercial life and transfer energy to higher/civic pursuits; deliberately choose activities that elevate character rather than glorify wealth accumulation.
